newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Storm lashes northern New Zealand, closes roads.
newsitem.headline: Storm lashes northern New Zealand, closes roads.

text.p: A storm carrying heavy rains and winds up to 130 km/hour (80 mph) lashed New Zealand's North Island on Monday and flash floods, landslips and snow closed roads across the central area by nightfall.
The Meteorological Service warned that up to 100 mm (four inches) of rain could fall, especially in the winegrowing Hawke's Bay region but also further south.
The Wairoa District Council closed a highway on both sides of the east coast town due to landslides and declared a local state of emergency, Radio New Zealand reported.
A council spokesman told TVNZ television news that roads had been blocked by land slips and flooding both towards Gisborne in the north and Napier to the south.
There were no reports of any casualties though a number of drivers had to be rescued from stranded and flooding vehicles across several areas of North Island.
Civil defence authorities in Hawke's Bay were monitoring roads and rivers and contacting homes at risk.
About 45 houses had been evacuated by mid-evening, TVNZ said.
The meteorological service, which has been issuing rain and high wind warnings since Saturday evening as the system approached, said winds would likely ease only slowly on Tuesday.
As the storm moved south over the capital Wellington and into the Cook Strait separating the North and South Islands by late Monday, the service was still predicting gusts of up to 130 km/hour.
